body: The “Salsa Revival: Bridging Generations” panel, held during the first day of Billboard Latin Music Week , brought together two generations of salsa artists: Tito Nieves and Luis Figueroa . The conversation took place Monday (Oct. 19) at the Faena Theater in Miami Beach and was moderated by Bryant Pino of AARP. Nieves, who has racked up numerous hits over the course of five decades — including “Fabricando Fantasías,” “De Mí Enamórate” and “El Amor Más Bonito” — shared the panel with Figueroa, who was born in Philadelphia but grew up listening to salsa at home and represents the genre’s new generation. “Young people inspire me. New York law requires a defamation lawsuit against a public figure to plead “actual malice” — that is, demonstrate that they lied on purpose. title: Quevedo & Kidd Voodoo Talk New Urban Movement: ‘One of the Things That Makes Us Unique Is Where We Come From’
summary: From the Canary Islands and Chile, the artists discussed identity and the global expansion of their respective scenes during Billboard Latin Music Week.
body: Urban music no longer moves in just one direction. It travels across islands, continents and platforms, absorbing local sounds and transforming them into global anthems. That was one of the central ideas of The New Urban Movement, a conversation featuring Quevedo and Kidd Voodoo on Monday (Oct. 19) during Billboard Latin Music Week 2026 . Moderated by Billboard associate editor Jessica Roiz, the panel took place at the Faena Theater in Miami Beach. Both artists discussed how their places of origin have shaped their music. “One of the things that makes us unique is where we come from,” Quevedo said. For him, growing up in the Canary Islands — a territory historically connected to Latin America — was essential to developing the identity of Buenas Noches (2024) and El Baifo (2026), an urban album that also incorporates merengue, salsa and other Latin rhythms. “Talking about our own experiences makes us artists more unique,” he added. title: Google is giving you more creative control over Gemini Notebook’s video overviews and slides
summary: Google will soon roll out "co-creation" capabilities for two of Gemini Notebook's most popular features.
body: Credit: Karandeep Singh / Android Authority TL;DR Gemini Notebook is giving users more creative control over Slide Decks and Video Overviews through a feature called “Co-creation.” The platform will now walk the user through the creation flow, allowing them to steer the format and visual style before the final output. Co-creation capabilities will roll out to all users over the upcoming week. Gemini Notebook is a helpful tool for digesting large amounts of information. One way this is done is by breaking down your material into structured formats such as Audio Overviews and Study Aids, like flashcards. After a new update, you’ll soon have more creative control over the output from two of these formats. In a blog post , Google announced that it will add “co-creation” capabilities to Video Overviews and Slide Decks. Normally, Gemini Notebook will take a prompt and jump right to the final product. However, with co-creation, Notebook will walk you through the creation flow before outputting a result.

title: TP-Link signs deal to produce Wi-Fi 8 routers in US amid FCC ban
summary: Starting early next year, Wi-Fi 8 routers will be assembled by Key Tronic in Mississippi.
body: TL;DR TP-Link signs letter of intent with Key Tronic to build Wi-Fi 8 routers in Mississippi. Manufacture will begin early next year. TP-Link continues to pursue exemption from FCC ban while it faces lawsuits. The impact of the ban on foreign-made routers that the FCC implemented in March is still causing reverberations. While some router manufacturers have received exemptions , one of the largest, TP-Link is not among them. Now the company looks like it might have found a way to keep selling routers in the United States. TP-Link has announced a partnership with tech manufacturer Key Tronic Corporation to assemble its products in the United States, beginning with production of its Wi-Fi 8 routers in Mississippi (via PCMag ). Production will begin “as early as next year.”

title: Straight Talk is giving its unlimited plans a boost without raising prices
summary: More hotspot data, faster 5G for some, and not a price hike in sight.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Straight Talk has upgraded its unlimited plans without increasing its monthly base prices. The $45 Silver plan now includes 5G Ultra Wideband, while Silver and Gold get more hotspot data. Customers also benefit from expanded international perks and savings on Home Internet bundles. It’s not often that your mobile carrier gives you extra without asking for more money in return. Straight Talk is bucking that trend with the latest refresh of its unlimited plans , adding more hotspot data, international benefits, and faster 5G access to its cheapest tier, all without raising monthly base prices. According to a Verizon press release , the biggest winner is the $45-per-month Silver Unlimited plan, which now includes access to 5G Ultra Wideband. Verizon claims this offers speeds three times faster than standard 5G. The $55 Gold and $65 Platinum plans already had Ultra Wideband access, so this is a particularly welcome upgrade for Silver subscribers, who haven’t seen their plan’s base price increase since 2009.

title: This magnetic accessory brings true flash back to phones
summary: The $85 accessory is iPhone-only for now, but Godox says Android support is coming.
body: TL;DR The $85 Godox A2 brings real xenon flash to smartphones. It’s iPhone-only for now, but the company says Android support is “under development.” Android devices led the way with built-in xenon flash, but abandoned the idea over a decade ago. For as outdated as it is, the image of a flashbulb going off as a button is pressed is one of the most universally recognizable signs of a photo being taken. And yet, our phones, which capture the majority of our photos , use LED flashes that don’t produce the same blinding intensity of light (or image quality) that are the result of “real” flash. But they can with the just introduced Godox A2, an accessory that uses a xenon flash tube and magnetically attaches to phones. The Godox A2 sells for $85, but don’t expect to order one for your Android device in the near future (via The Verge ). It’s iPhone-only for now, though on the product page, the company says that Android support is “under development.” Because the Godox A2 relies on a magnetic connection, like Apple’s MagSafe, it won’t work with every Android device. title: Google Play Store bug is causing Collections confusion

It has been about two years since Google introduced the Play Store feature known as “ Collections .” This feature organizes your apps by topic and highlights content recommended by your apps.
